title: fix(skills): refresh skills after watched directories are replaced
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes stale Skills content after a watched directory is replaced while another watcher still holds the old filesystem identity.

## User Impact

On Node Linux and Windows, later edits to the replacement directory refresh Skills without restarting OpenClaw. No configuration change is required. macOS, Bun and polling retain the stock Chokidar route.

## Why This Change Was Made

Skills now owns shallow native directory registrations on Linux and Windows. It acquires observation before scanning, carries the identity proven by native admission, fences invalidated scan work, and joins scans and registration retirement during close. Existing path admission and event stability policy remain in use. Chokidar stays unmodified; this change adds no dependency patch, fork or upgrade.

The shared watcher contract lives in a type-only leaf, so the transport and native implementation do not form a static import cycle. Windows fixtures account for the retired generation's required missing-root error and verify replacement discovery followed by an edit to the same cached skill.

Production net increase: 780 lines; tests counted separately. This owns the registration, scan and retirement lifecycle previously delegated to shared dependency state.

## Evidence

Current signed head: `e1cd13471f91`. The bounded corrective source review is clean. Targeted formatting and diff checks passed. Current-source standalone runs passed 317 cases with one named platform skip across 13 files. A four-file joint run with one worker passed all 62 cases with no skips. Architecture, core and services typechecks, focused lint, formatting, source ratchets and dead-export checks passed. `pnpm build` passed in 23m 41s. Native preparation is complete. The first exact-head hosted CI attempt finished with 171 passing jobs, 13 skips, one UI E2E pin-click failure and its aggregate failure; all five Windows rows and architecture passed. The unchanged-head failed-jobs rerun was deferred before UI execution by [Full Release Validation priority](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35984021515). After release priority cleared, the maintained full rerun restored preflight and its matrix. Attempt 3 has passed all nine UI E2E jobs. The [actual UI row 2 rerun](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35981091604/job/107627709809) tested merge `4984c48f5338` on Node 24.21.0 with three workers: all 11 target-file cases and all 358 shard cases passed. Although the job label is 2/9, the recorded command used `--shard 2/8`. This is a same-source passing rerun, not a diagnosed UI cause or a UI source change. Attempt 3 finished with 171 successful jobs, 13 skips, and only the native Windows row 2 Scheduled Task fixture failure plus its dependent aggregate failure. The separate fixture repair https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/157289 has landed as 440ec7d538f5e95042569a102437ee05b2a6e8e4 after its focused native, standalone and production-budget unit proof passed. Attempt 4 completed successfully with 173 successful jobs and 13 skips. Its fresh Windows row 2 job and dependent aggregate passed; the other 171 successes and 13 skips were inherited. The retry tested the original merge 4984c48f5338, not the newly fixed fixture: the native Scheduled Task case passed in 1.838 seconds with both missing and registered/found results, without the registration-unavailable early return. This qualifies the unchanged Skills head without establishing the earlier timeout's cause. The exact-head required CI, dependency and security statuses are green. The exact-head ClawSweeper review completed with no code or security findings. Maintainer decision: accept the Node Linux/Windows native route based on the source-bound Linux proof and the real Windows delete/recreate plus settled same-file cached edit below.

A bounded diagnostic on the failed CI merge `4984c48f5338`, with temporary tracing only, passed the complete 11-case UI file with no skips in 37.424s wrapper time. All eight click markers completed. This is focused non-reproduction, not concurrent-shard equivalence or a source fix; truncated protocol records prevent missing-reply inferences. The temporary instrumentation remains unpublished.

The [current native Windows job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35981091604/job/107573507634) passed on the actual merged tree `4984c48f5338` containing this head. Both real higher/intermediate ancestor cases executed (3.215s / 2.911s): delete/recreate the watched directory, settle and prime the cached loader, then edit the same SKILL.md and observe the new description. The two ancestor cases use native Windows filesystem callbacks, with Node 24.20.0 and four workers. Windows uses delete/recreate because live handles prevent the same-turn ancestor rename. The initially missing root and all four prior held-sibling callback fixtures also passed.

The earlier `0df32a99d617` proof passed 67 affected tests and the strict original-owner negative control, plus types, scoped checks and build. Earlier runtime evidence retains 363 passes and one named platform skip. These measurements and reviews remain bound to their original sources and toolchains; they are not current-head qualification. Injected Windows callback cases prove the callback contract, not native Windows filesystem behavior.


Current runs used Linux/x64, Node 24.19.0, pnpm 12.4.2, TypeScript 7.0.2 and Vitest 5.0.1. Each standalone command was `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <file> --maxWorkers=1 --retry=0` with verbose/JSON reporters. Wrapper wall time includes the repository wrapper; Vitest wall time is its reported duration. Paths below are under `src/skills/runtime/` unless shown otherwise.

The six historical measurements used Node 24.19.0, pnpm 12.4.0 and Vitest 5.0.0; their TypeScript version was not recorded. Four historical files retain identical bytes. The content-watch and rescan-gap files changed only their type-import location, with isolated emitted-code equivalence checked; these remain historical timings. The two support files are not runnable tests. These are standalone Linux costs, not per-file hosted CI costs. The failed [historical 7137 Windows job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35970226138/job/107538478325) recorded group-only costs of 46.64s Vitest, 51.46s wrapper and 134s job time; these cannot be apportioned to individual files. The current Windows Skills-containing 16-file group passed 194 cases with 19 platform skips in 63.95s Vitest time. Its whole job took 482s and continued through later tooling/plugin groups; the historical 134s job stopped at the failing Skills-containing group. These observations do not isolate watcher overhead, and the whole-job totals are not comparable.

Hosted timing rank-up: standalone per-file costs and actual grouped CI costs are supplied above. Per-file hosted wall time is unavailable from the grouped logs, so that finer measurement is skipped; no inferred allocation or additional timing-only rerun is used.

Two private collectors failed after successful test execution: one rejected Vitest's `639ms` duration and one compared JSON lists with tuples. Both failed receipts are retained unchanged; complete raw reports, logs, managed joins and exact source/dependency bindings were independently checked. The nine affected checks and build passed separately on the same signed head.

## Follow-up Boundaries

- Native macOS watcher continuity across overlapping generations needs separate proof.
- A standalone symbolic-root retarget enrolls its new physical target through normal watcher preparation.
- Alias-only Windows metadata notifications need separate investigation; no introduced regression or native Windows reproduction was established.
- Generation-owned symlink relevance needs separate repair; source tracing found the same classification race in the stock transport.
- Restartless recovery and availability notifications after watcher failures are separate work.
